title: Preserve the first-start boundary for later own-command placement descriptions
outcome: A repeated start or later runs-there description cannot hide a command that began before a check's terminal by using the later description tick as its execution start.
acceptance: A deterministic regression covers a write-capable command first placed outside a check's worktree, then placed into it after the check's terminal while its closing capture is pending; evidence stays conservative for actual overlap.
Repeated starts and runs-there descriptions use a defensible first-start boundary or an equivalent conservative rule, while ordinary strictly serial command completion descriptions retain credit.
The exact changed input has a passing full gate and clean independent review pair.
